extracted.intended_audience: Registration Agencies, State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), program sponsors, OA staff, State CTE Agencies, and other National Apprenticeship System stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory requirements and quality/data standards governing registration, oversight, data collection, reporting, exemptions, and State agency roles for registered apprenticeship and CTE apprenticeship programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deregistration for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.24(g)(5): provide for the deregistration of programs that fail to meet the requirements of this subpart; process for deregistration would be the same as the process in proposed §29.20 of subpart A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A program review would occur to ascertain a sponsor's compliance with this subpart and part 30. The Department emphasizes alignment of deregistration proceedings with subpart A to enable effective oversight of registered apprenticeship programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearings process alignment for deregistration and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.24(g)(6) and (7): provide the same hearings process as described in proposed §29.21 in subpart A for registration and deregistration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because both models (subparts A and B) have similar processes, the Department proposes to align hearing processes to minimize parallel processes and seeks comments on administrative efficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and role of Registration Agencies for CTE apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.24(g)(8): Registration Agencies would be responsible for registration of CTE apprenticeship programs; Registration Agencies may be OA or a recognized SAA; requirement for a written agreement between the State CTE Agency and the Registration Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department envisions localized alignment with State/local education systems and anticipates local registration by the State's Registration Agency; OA considered only in States without a recognized SAA and with a written agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit registration authority to entities registering under subpart A
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.24(g)(8)(ii): limit ability to be a Registration Agency for CTE apprenticeship to those entities that are Registration Agencies for registering apprenticeship programs under subpart A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to ensure alignment at the State level so entities approving registered apprenticeship programs under subpart A are the same approving CTE apprenticeship programs under subpart B, minimizing redundancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAA recognition criterion: state laws protect safety and welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.24(g)(8)(ii)(A): the State's proposed or current apprenticeship laws for registered CTE apprenticeship must meet or exceed the requirements for protecting the safety and welfare of CTE apprentices set forth in subpart B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors the standard for SAAs seeking recognition under subpart C; SAAs may adopt additional protections beyond the federal minimums.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAA recognition criterion: written agreement with State CTE Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.24(g)(8)(ii)(B): the SAA must have entered into a written agreement with the respective State CTE Agency outlining required coordination, roles, and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement allows the Administrator to ensure necessary coordination is occurring at the State level for CTE apprenticeship registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAA recognition criterion: submission of laws and CTE engagement strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.24(g)(8)(ii)(C): the State has submitted its relevant apprenticeship laws and CTE engagement strategies as part of its State Apprenticeship Plan per proposed §29.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission may be concurrent with recognition under subpart C or as a modification under §29.27(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: SAA recognition criterion: Administrator approval for SAA recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.24(g)(8)(ii)(D): the Administrator must approve concurrently, or have previously approved, the State government agency for recognition as an SAA under proposed §29.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures entities registering under subpart B are approved to register programs under subpart A purposes; a State government agency may serve as an SAA only for subpart A purposes unless otherwise recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align data collection and use of RAPIDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.24(g)(9): align data collection from sponsors and SAAs with requirements in proposed §29.25 and anticipate utilizing RAPIDS as the primary database and case management system for collection and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department may improve or alter RAPIDS over time; technical assistance provided by OA, Apprenticeship Training Representatives, and SAA staff. SAA States and sponsors may voluntarily opt to use Department's system.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprentice data: collect associated industry skills framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.24(g)(9)(i)(A): for registered CTE apprenticeship, collect an associated industry skills framework with the program rather than the occupation associated with registered apprenticeship under §29.25(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects subpart B's unique requirement that associated industry skills frameworks form the basis for training in CTE apprenticeship. The Department is not proposing to collect pre-apprenticeship participation information here as a regulatory requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE reporting cadence: academic semester updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed paragraph (g)(9)(i)(B): sponsors to report status updates on an academic semester basis rather than within 30 days for CTE apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This adjustment accounts for the unique nature of CTE apprenticeship models where sponsors are largely from the education system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program sponsor information and outcome metrics for CTE
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.24(g)(9)(ii): collect sponsor information and quality metrics by industry skills framework and collect outcomes including placement into registered apprenticeship under subpart A, postsecondary educational program, or employment at program completion (employment meaning outside subpart A apprenticeship employment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables measurement of outcomes specific to CTE apprenticeship and alignment with subpart A reporting structures where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reporting of collected information
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.24(g)(9)(iii) and §29.25(c): information and reports based on collected data to be made publicly available by the Registration Agency, including State and sponsor-level reporting and a national summary report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligned with §29.28 reporting for SAAs; intended to support comprehensive system data and transparency but balanced against privacy and burden concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions procedure and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.24(g)(10) (and reference to §29.23): requests for exemptions from subpart B requirements must be in writing, state reasons, and are granted by the Administrator only for good cause. Exemptions cannot be made for requirements outside this subpart or other applicable Federal, State, or local laws (e.g., Perkins program requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of good cause are discussed in preamble to §29.23; Department added language clarifying non-waivable statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsors must report apprentice and sponsor information to Registration Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.25: formalize requirements for sponsors to report apprentice and sponsor information to their Registration Agency and establish requirement for Department to make sponsor-level and national summary reports publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting primarily through RAPIDS or equivalent Registration Agency case management system; Department interested in comments about burden, privacy, and whether the approach strikes the proper balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual apprentice data elements and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.25(a): collect individual apprentice information including demographic data and require sponsors to report, within 30 days of a change, start date of on-the-job training, changes to credentials attained, employment retention, and wage progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department exploring mechanisms for apprentices to self-report demographic information directly. Collection enables cross-sectional analyses, disaggregation for DEIA, and program quality assessments. Department will follow applicable laws and procedures to ensure data security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of uniform data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Rationale in preamble to §29.25: uniform collection enables substantive program analyses (DEIA, best practices, economic mobility), reduces burden on employers, and ensures consistent questioning of apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department seeks comments on ability to collect individualized data and strategies to assess program performance in standardized manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor reporting timing and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.25(b): paragraph (b)(1) requires sponsors to update certain items within 30 days of status change; paragraph (b)(2) requires annual updates and certification by sponsors of items in the Department system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors using Department-provided system should ensure records are current and accurate and then certify in that system. Sponsors not using Department system must submit and certify in the Department system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual public information and balancing privacy/burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §29.25(b)(2) the Department anticipates annual information will be made publicly available to assist job seekers; seeks comments on appropriate amount of information given burdens and privacy protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department proposes mostly using measures a Registration Agency can calculate on behalf of a sponsor to avoid unique manual tracking burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure to detect programs exiting apprentices without graduation
rubrics_metrics.description: New measure proposed in §29.25(b)(2): a measure to help Registration Agencies see if programs are exiting significant numbers of apprentices and not graduating them; unlike cohort completion rate, this measure would not exclude exiters during the probationary period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for use in program reviews under §29.19 and aligned with Department's ETP reporting under WIOA. Department requests comments on whether probationary exits should be included and other measure design questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure: percentage of exiters entering postsecondary or career pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.25(b)(2)(viii): a measure to determine the percentage of exiters who enter a postsecondary educational program or a career pathway program at time of exit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps identify articulation with postsecondary systems, important for youth and sectors like health care and education; Department recognizes small percentages in some industries but values disaggregation by industry and occupation.

rubrics_metrics.name: System-level income performance reporting measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.25(c): Department is considering a system-level performance reporting measure set at 200 percent of the Federal poverty level to quantify income outcomes for apprentices in the year after program completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an individual receives at least 200% FPL in the year after completion this would be considered a successful outcome; Department invites comments on methodology and how to define successful income outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withholding or suppressing data from publication for good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed paragraph (c)(5): Department may decide to withhold information from publication for good cause (e.g., risk of PII attribution, inaccurate data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department may omit/suppress data elements to protect PII or sponsor-requested confidential elements; will provide operational guidance through subregulatory guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of supplemental information sources for system metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.25(c)(3): Registration Agencies should use supplemental sources (surveys, wage records, etc.) to calculate system-level quality metrics and provide necessary sources and technical assistance to sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental sources enable calculation of metrics such as post-apprenticeship employment retention (6 and 12 months), annualized median earnings of exited apprentices, percent of completers earning income allowing them to support families one year after completion, and customer service metrics for Registration Agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research, evaluation, and suppression protocols for public products
rubrics_metrics.description: Department will conduct research and longitudinal studies to assess program impact and may omit/suppress data in publicly facing products to protect apprentice PII or sponsor-requested confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department will provide guidance and operational protocol through subregulatory guidance; seeks comments on measures and measurement framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities of State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.26: substantially revise duties of SAAs; clarify that recognized SAAs possess the exclusive, non-delegable authority to evaluate, approve, register, monitor, oversee, suspend, and deregister apprenticeship programs within the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies allocation between SAAs and State Apprenticeship Councils; SAAs act as impartial governmental bodies accountable to elected executive authority and can serve as laboratories for innovative models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that State Apprenticeship Councils operate under SAA direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Preamble discussion referencing existing 29 CFR 29.13(a)(2): a State Apprenticeship Council must be established by an SAA and operate under the direction of that SAA; SAAs should not cede authority to councils or external entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department notes complaints where Councils impermissibly exercised authority (e.g., infrequent hearings, lack of due process, denial without written record) and intends to ensure procedural due process and avoid barriers to registration.
